A. Sesa Care Private Limited: Dabur India Limited (Dabur) has entered into an Implementation Agreement (IA) with the shareholders of Sesa Care Private Limited (Sesa) and Sesa for undertaking necessary steps for commencement of merger of Sesa with Dabur.
As a part of the Transaction, prior to the completion of the merger of Sesa with Dabur:
a) Dabur shall acquire 51% of the paid up Cumulative Redeemable Preference Shares of Sesa from its existing shareholders; and
b) Dabur shall extend a Corporate Guarantee for the loans availed / to be availed by Sesa from various lenders.
B. Sesa Care Bangladesh Private Limited: Sesa also has a wholly owned subsidiary in Bangladesh, viz. Sesa Care Bangladesh Pvt. Ltd. Upon completion of the merger, the said entity shall become a wholly owned subsidiary of Dabur.
The above transaction was approved by the Board of Directors of the Company in their meeting held on October 30, 2024 and the said intimation was also filed with the Stock Exchanges under Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 on October 30, 2024.
During the quarter ended March 31, 2025: (a) Dabur had on January 10, 2025, acquired 1,25,90,070 Cumulative Redeemable Preference Shares, comprising of 51% of the total paid up Preference Share Capital of Sesa from its existing shareholders for a total consideration of Rs.12,59,00,700/-. (b) Dabur had extended Corporate Guarantees towards loans/ facilities availed by Sesa and the same have become effective on January 10, 2025, upon drawdown of loans/ facilities by Sesa. The said acquisition and extending of corporate guarantee was informed to the Stock Exchanges on January 10, 2025 under Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.

xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: Additional Commissioner, CGST Commissionerate, Chandigarh, had issued a order confirming a total demand of Rs. 3,20,60,53,070/- as IGST under Section 20 of the IGST Act, 2017, read with Section 74(9) of CGST Act, 2017 and corresponding Section of State GST Act, 2017, along with interest payable thereon under Section 20 of the IGST Act, 2017, read with Section 50 of CGST Act, 2017 and corresponding Section of State GST Act, 2017. The Additional Commissioner has dropped the penalty imposed under their earlier intimation.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Company has filed appeal(s) before the 1st appellate authority.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Office of the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Circle 7(1), Delhi.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: The Company has received an Income-tax re-assessment Order for the FY 2017-18 wherein an income tax demand of Rs. 110.33 crores has been made under Section 156 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 ("the Act"). The demand is due to impact of re-assessment proceedings under Section 263 of the Act. It has been alleged by the Income Tax Authority that the Company has wrongly claimed tax deduction on In-house Research and Development and Section 14A of the Act.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Company has filed an appeal before CIT(Appeals) against the said Demand Order in April 2025. As regards the demand, the Company apart from CIT (Appeals) has also filed rectification petition under Section 154 in April 2025 to rectify the computation of demand, by which the demand may be reduced significantly. The Company has also filed application with the Tax authorities for stay of demand. The Company is of the opinion that it has strong merits in the case, as the substantial part of the demand has been computed inadvertently by including income which was earlier already added in original 143(3) order for AY 2018-19. Also, the demand for Rs. 36.77 crores have been raised without any discussions in the order. Further, for the balance demand arising out of disallowances on in-house Research and Development and Section 14A of the Act, given the merits, the Company has a strong case. Financial implication due to this Order is unlikely. The implication, if any, will be limited to the extent of final demand towards tax as may be ascertained by higher forums.
